title: 1997 AHSME Problem 19
statement: A circle with center \(O\) is tangent to the coordinate axes and to the hypotenuse of the \(30^\circ\)-\(60^\circ\)-\(90^\circ\) triangle \(ABC\) as shown, where \(AB=1.\) To the nearest hundredth, what is the radius of the circle?

solutions.text: Take \(A=(0,0),\) \(B=(1,0),\) and \(C=(0,\sqrt3).\) The hypotenuse is \(\sqrt3x+y=\sqrt3,\) and the circle center is \(O=(r,r).\) Tangency gives \[ \frac{\left|(\sqrt3+1)r-\sqrt3\right|}{2}=r. \] The pictured external circle has \((\sqrt3+1)r-\sqrt3=2r,\) so \(r=\frac{\sqrt3}{\sqrt3-1}\) \(=\frac{3+\sqrt3}{2}\approx2.37.\) Thus D is correct.
hints: If the circle radius is \(r\), then \(O=(r,r)\) in the displayed coordinates
Write the hypotenuse line of the \(30^\circ\)-\(60^\circ\)-\(90^\circ\) triangle and set its distance from \(O\) equal to \(r\)
